flags.title: Unstable or stable angina?
flags.concern: The clinician suspects unstable angina but plans outpatient cardiology next week; the described pattern (three months, only on walking, pain-free at rest) fits stable angina better, and if it is truly unstable the outpatient timeline is too slow.
flags.consider: Consider clarifying rest pain or a crescendo pattern and, if present, same-day ED evaluation with troponin; otherwise consider labelling it stable angina with expedited outpatient work-up.

evidence.quote: my suspicion is you have something called unstable angina
we will try to get you into cardiology the next week
it mainly happens when i'm walking

flags.title: Echocardiogram for murmur with exertional chest pain?
flags.concern: A 2/6 systolic ejection murmur with exertional chest pain and ankle edema raises the possibility of aortic stenosis, which can cause angina and affects stress test safety.
flags.consider: Consider an echocardiogram before or alongside the stress test.

evidence.quote: you do have a two over six systolic ejection murmur
get you set up for some sort of a stress test

flags.title: Thiazide as first agent with diabetes?
flags.concern: Hydrochlorothiazide was started in a patient with diabetes, where thiazides can worsen glucose and potassium, before hypertension was confirmed and without checking allergies despite the sulfa warning.
flags.consider: Consider confirming the diagnosis with home readings, checking for sulfa allergy and baseline electrolytes and creatinine, and whether an ACE inhibitor or ARB would suit her better.

sometimes you can have a cross reaction with some other medications like sulfa medications

flags.title: Statin and lipid panel not addressed?
flags.concern: A 53-year-old with diabetes and suspected coronary disease would usually qualify for statin therapy, but lipids and statins were not discussed.
flags.consider: Consider checking a lipid panel and starting a statin.
